why: CountDevices is read and the insert happens afterwards with no transaction or lock, so concurrent requests can all pass the count >= deviceLimit check and exceed the limit.
Authenticate now calls TagDevice synchronously and returns ErrDeviceLimitReached as an auth failure (lines 44-47); TagDevice was changed to propagate the tagging error (impl.go line 147).
rowsAffected == 0 is mapped to ErrDeviceLimitReached, although it only means no existing device matched the id/time window.
The BETWEEN bounds are computed from device.UpdatedAt rather than time.Now(), unlike the CountDevices window in CreateOrUpdateDevice.
localCache.SetDefault runs before CreateOrUpdateDevice, so a device rejected with ErrDeviceLimitReached stays cached and skips the limit check for 29 minutes.
Cached permissions are trusted only when they allow (lines 123-136); a cached deny falls through to a fresh DB lookup, so a stale cached grant still allows access after revocation.
Test file (not in methods_read): the comment says the cached permissions allow access but the map stores false for dashboards:uid:dash1.
The denial key joins namespace, user, action, name and parent with underscores, so values containing underscores or empty parts can collide.
Each method dereferences req.PluginContext (lines 40, 45, 50, 55) with no req == nil guard, unlike LoggerMiddleware, so a nil request panics.
logRequest no longer adds traceID to logParams, and the new instrumentContext does not add it either, so plugin request logs lose the trace ID.
FromContext returns NewTestLogger() instead of the receiver, so logs written through it are lost to test assertions.

applyTemplateVariables is called with request.filters, but the shardQuerySplitting tests mock it as a one-argument function, so the filters path is untested; the same call is in runSplitQuery line 299 (file choice is ambiguous).
The grafana case renders GrafanaRuleListItem inside rules.map without key={key} (the other cases keep it).

SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer renders only when rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule), but GrafanaRuleListItem (line 47) now passes only promRule, so 'Silence notifications' sets state and shows nothing.
klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log) uses the base logger instead of the enriched log with name/kind/method.

In DeleteCollection the legacy DeleteCollection duration is recorded with recordStorageDuration instead of recordLegacyDuration; the comment's wording is garbled, and Create (line 45) and Update (line 129) have the inverse mix-up.
recordStorageDuration is passed name instead of options.Kind as the kind label.
Debug output (ids, counts, cond) is logged with r.log.Error on every batch (lines 534, 537, 554, 557 and 576, 579).
The cleanup ticker changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute, running every cleanup job ten times as often.
After acquiring the write lock it does not re-check entryPointAssetsCache, so goroutines that queued on the lock all re-read the assets.
entryPointAssetsCache = result runs even when the read failed, overwriting a valid cache with nil.
Both branches return false (lines 195-199), so ReadQuery always rejects SQL expressions.
The replacement for go-duck is stubs that return 'not implemented' (lines 13, 17, 21), so TablesList and SQLCommand.Execute always fail.
cacheMu now guards only the final b.cache[key] assignment, so concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same key both build the index.
init calls s.search.TotalDocs() after starting the event watcher goroutine; TotalDocs (bleve.go line 146) ranges over b.cache without cacheMu while BuildIndex can write it.
